text: I have four decades of digital art experience. There was no AI when I started. I use generative AI for experimentation, but my creative outputs still come from my own secret technique, which I developed in my twenties over thirty years ago. question: Q6.2 Identity & purpose
text: AI doesn't threaten my sense of identity as a creative professional. It reshapes the terrain I work on. The core of my identity isn't "person who produces outputs" but "person who notices things, cares about them, and tries to say something true." AI can generate variations, drafts, and options at scale, but it can't want anything. It can't care. The wanting and the caring are where my identity lives. If my purpose were purely throughput, churning out assets, AI would rightly destabilise that. But purpose in creative work has always been more about judgment, taste, and meaning making: knowing what's worth making, why it matters, and for whom. AI raises the floor on execution, which actually raises the ceiling on what's expected of taste and intention. That's uncomfortable, but it's not nihilistic.
